title: BC/DR Testing Hierarchy
objective: Study-guide review — CISSP — Domain 6: Security Assessment and Testing: BC/DR Testing Hierarchy.

items: DR plans must be tested regularly to ensure they work when needed
Tests range from least disruptive (tabletop) to most disruptive (full-scale)
A manager must know which test type is appropriate based on maturity and risk tolerance
More disruptive tests provide higher confidence but carry greater operational risk
Testing should progress from least to most disruptive as the plan matures

rows: Distribute plan copies for review; individuals verify their roles and responsibilities
Key personnel discuss the plan in a conference room, walking through scenarios verbally. No systems are actually tested
Team members walk through the plan step by step, verifying each procedure on paper. More detailed than tabletop but still discussion-based
Team simulates a disaster scenario and practices response procedures. May involve some operational components but does not affect production
DR systems are brought online at the recovery site while primary systems continue to run. Verifies the recovery site can support operations without disrupting production
Primary systems are actually shut down and operations transfer to the recovery site. The only test that fully validates the DR plan

blocks.text: From Destination CISSP: "Parallel Test — DR plan at recovery site/on parallel systems. Full-interruption/Full-scale — Cause an actual disaster and follow DR plan to restore systems and data." Key Manager Decision Framework:

items: New/untested plan → Start with checklist review or tabletop
Maturing plan → Progress to walkthrough and simulation
Validated plan → Parallel test (low risk to production)
Full confidence needed → Full-scale test (high risk, highest assurance)

blocks.title: Exam trap
blocks.text: ⚠️ Exam Trap: A parallel test brings the recovery site online BUT production systems continue to run — there is NO actual disruption to operations. A full-scale test actually SHUTS DOWN production — it's the only test that truly validates the plan but carries the most risk. ⚠️ Exam Trap: The exam loves scenario questions: "The organization has never tested its DR plan. Which test should they start with?" Answer: Tabletop exercise — least disruptive, allows team to identify gaps before risking operational systems.
